surfaces.part: flat zinc roof plates with riveted seams

answer.evidence: The roof is a large plate plane (rows 4-16, 13 rows) on a 30-32 px wide body. It ends in a bright front-edge line at row 17 (L=202), followed by dark eave shadow at rows 18-19 (L=71, then 21). Below it is the front wall with the door and firewood, rows 20-30 (11 rows). The stovepipe is a thin shaft with a cone cap at rows 0-3, which widens 3-5-7-9 and so reads as a sloped cap. The roof has no visible receding side face, so the view is south-facing 3/4.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small hut, about 2x1.5 tiles, so it is much smaller than the two reference houses. Its measured density matches them: 14 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, 3% near-flat coverage against 0%, and only 1% neutral dark edge pixels. That means the outline is a tinted dark blue-green and brown line beside the metal and wood, not a black sticker line. By eye, the roof plates, rivets, seams, stovepipe with cone cap, door and orange firewood ends are all separated by value, and no large flat block shows. Shading is somewhat shallower than the references, at about 4 steps per material against 5-6, because only 23 colours cover the whole piece. That is acceptable for a prop this size. A careful artist would accept it next to the references without it looking flatter or more sticker-like.
